scholarships.name: Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship
scholarships.hostUniversities: University of Toronto (all three campuses: St. George, Mississauga, Scarborough)
scholarships.fundingSummary: Covers full tuition, books, incidental fees, and full residence support for four years of undergraduate study at the University of Toronto.
benefits: Access to Pearson community and events
eligibility: International student (non-Canadian) requiring a study permit
Currently in final year of secondary school or have graduated no earlier than June 2025
Demonstrated exceptional academic achievement (high 90s average recommended)
Demonstrated leadership and community involvement
Creative, innovative and impactful in your school and community
Must be nominated by your high school (schools must have a Pearson nomination form)
documentsRequired: University of Toronto online application for admission
Pearson Scholarship application (separate from UofT application)
List of extracurricular activities and leadership roles
scholarships.deadlineNote: School nomination deadline late September; student application deadline late November; supporting documents early December.
scholarships.durationNote: 4 years undergraduate (renewable annually based on academic standing)
thingsToHaveBeforeApply: School nomination from your high school

scholarships.name: UBC International Leader of Tomorrow Award
scholarships.hostUniversities: University of British Columbia (Vancouver and Okanagan campuses)
scholarships.fundingSummary: Covers partial to full tuition based on financial need, renewable for up to 4 years of undergraduate study at UBC.
benefits: Tuition costs covered based on demonstrated financial need (up to full tuition)
Renewable for up to 3 additional years
Awarded in combination with the UBC International Major Entrance Scholarship
Access to UBC's global alumni network
eligibility: International student entering UBC from a secondary school
Demonstrated outstanding academic achievement
Demonstrated leadership through extracurricular activities and community involvement
Demonstrated financial need that would otherwise prevent study at UBC
First-time undergraduate applicant (not a transfer student)
Must meet UBC's English language admission requirement
documentsRequired: List of extracurricular and leadership activities
scholarships.deadlineNote: UBC admission application deadline is January 15; scholarship considered automatically based on admission application personal profile.
thingsToHaveBeforeApply: English proficiency test results (IELTS 6.5+ or TOEFL 90+)

scholarships.name: Yale University Scholarships for International Students
scholarships.fundingSummary: 100% demonstrated need-based financial aid covering full tuition, room, board, travel, and health insurance for all four years.
benefits: Full tuition fees covered (100% of demonstrated need)
Travel allowance (one round-trip per year for international students)
Access to Yale's global alumni network
eligibility: International student of any nationality
Admitted to Yale College as a first-year undergraduate
Demonstrated financial need (Yale is need-blind for all applicants)
Strong academic record and standardized test scores
Leadership potential and community contribution
No separate scholarship application required (need-blind admission)
documentsRequired: Common Application or Coalition Application with Yale-specific questions
SAT or ACT scores (Yale is test-flexible)
TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo scores (for non-native English speakers)
CSS Profile and Yale Financial Aid Application
scholarships.deadlineNote: Single-choice early action November 1; regular decision January 2. Financial aid materials due same dates.
thingsToHaveBeforeApply: Strong high school grades (top 5-10% of class)

scholarships.name: MIT Scholarships for International Students
scholarships.fundingSummary: 100% need-based financial aid covering full tuition, room, board, and personal expenses for all four years at MIT.
benefits: Summer earnings expectation replaced by grant for international students
eligibility: International student of any nationality
Admitted to MIT as a first-year undergraduate
Demonstrated financial need (MIT is need-blind for international students)
Exceptional academic record in STEM and all subjects
Strong standardized test scores (SAT/ACT required)
Must demonstrate MIT's fit through essays, activities, and recommendations
documentsRequired: Secondary school transcripts and school report
SAT or ACT scores (required for all applicants)
TOEFL scores (recommended for non-native speakers, 90+ iBT)
CSS Profile and MIT International Student Financial Aid Application
Portfolio or research abstract (optional but recommended)
scholarships.deadlineNote: Early Action November 1; Regular Action January 6. Financial aid materials same deadlines.
scholarships.durationNote: 4 years undergraduate (renewable annually based on continued need)

scholarships.name: Oxford-Weidenfeld and Hoffmann Scholarship
scholarships.provider: Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Trust in partnership with University of Oxford
scholarships.fundingSummary: Covers full tuition, college fees, and a generous living costs grant for graduate study at Oxford, plus leadership development programming.
benefits: Full University of Oxford tuition and college fees
Living costs grant (sufficient for a single student in Oxford)
Invitation to exclusive events and seminars
eligibility: Citizen of a developing country (including Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, etc.)
Applying for an eligible one-year Master's course at Oxford
Demonstrated academic excellence (first-class or strong upper-second-class degree)
Commitment to public service, leadership, and contributing to your home country's development
Clear career goal linked to the development of your home country
Must apply for admission to Oxford and separately for the scholarship
documentsRequired: Proof of English language proficiency (IELTS 7.0+ required for most courses)
scholarships.deadlineNote: Scholarship deadline is early January; Oxford course deadlines are typically December or January.
thingsToHaveBeforeApply: A clear development impact goal for your home country
Oxford course choice and admission application prepared

scholarships.name: Scotland Saltire Scholarship
scholarships.provider: Scottish Government (administered by participating Scottish universities)
scholarships.hostUniversities: Participating Scottish universities (University of Edinburgh, University of Glasgow, University of St Andrews, University of Aberdeen, University of Strathclyde, etc.)
scholarships.fundingSummary: Provides a tuition fee waiver of up to £8,000 per year for a one-year Master's programme at a Scottish university.
benefits: Tuition fee waiver of up to £8,000
Covers one year of Master's study in Scotland
Available in any field of study
Can be combined with other university-specific scholarships
Open to citizens from eligible partner countries
eligibility: Citizen of an eligible partner country (India, Pakistan, USA, Canada, China, Japan, Hong Kong, South Korea, Indonesia, Malaysia, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Thailand, etc.)
Hold an offer of admission to a full-time Master's programme at a participating Scottish university
Demonstrate ability to pay remaining tuition and living costs
Meet the English language requirements of the university
Not previously enrolled in a Scottish university
scholarships.deadlineNote: Deadlines vary by university, typically May 31 for September intake. Check with your chosen university.
thingsToHaveBeforeApply: University admission offer from a participating Scottish university
Proof of eligible citizenship (e.g. Pakistani passport)

scholarships.name: Danish Government Scholarship for International Students
scholarships.provider: Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science
scholarships.hostUniversities: Participating Danish universities (University of Copenhagen, Aarhus University, Technical University of Denmark, University of Southern Denmark, Aalborg University, Roskilde University)
scholarships.fundingSummary: Covers full or partial tuition fees and provides a living stipend for a Master's programme at a Danish university.
benefits: Full or partial tuition fee waiver (varies by university)
Monthly living stipend (typically DKK 3,000-7,000 per month)
Access to Danish higher education system
eligibility: Non-EU/EEA citizen with a valid residence permit outside Denmark
Hold a Bachelor's degree equivalent to a Danish Bachelor's
Admitted to a Master's programme at a participating Danish university
Strong academic record (B+ average or higher)
Meet English language requirements (IELTS 6.5+ or TOEFL 88+)
Not already residing in Denmark
scholarships.deadlineNote: Deadlines vary by university (typically March 1 or April 1). Check individual university pages.
thingsToHaveBeforeApply: Motivation letter tailored to Danish education

scholarships.name: Finnish Government Scholarship Pool
scholarships.hostUniversities: Participating Finnish universities (University of Helsinki, Aalto University, University of Turku, University of Oulu, Tampere University, University of Eastern Finland)
scholarships.fundingSummary: Monthly stipend of €1,500-€2,000 for Master's/PhD study at a Finnish university; tuition fees must be covered separately.
benefits: Possible accommodation support from host university
eligibility: Non-Finnish citizen from an eligible country
Admitted to a Master's or PhD programme at a Finnish university
Excellent academic record
Meet the university's language requirements
Not already holding a residence permit in Finland
Applications submitted by the host university (not directly by students)
scholarships.deadlineNote: Deadlines vary by university; typically February-April for autumn intake. Universities nominate candidates to EDUFI.
thingsToHaveBeforeApply: Admission offer from a Finnish university
Contact a Finnish university's international office

scholarships.name: Amsterdam Merit Scholarship
scholarships.fundingSummary: Partial scholarship ranging from €6,000 to full tuition coverage for one year, renewable for a second year.
benefits: Scholarship of €6,000–€25,000 (full tuition) for one year
Possible renewal for a second year
Can be combined with other funding sources
eligibility: Non-EU/EEA international student
(Provisionally) admitted to a Master's programme at UvA
Excellent academic record (top 10-15% of your graduating class)
Meet UvA English language requirements (IELTS 6.5-7.0 / TOEFL 92-100)
No previous degree from UvA
Not eligible for Dutch government student finance
documentsRequired: AMS application form (submitted to UvA after admission)
scholarships.deadlineNote: Admission application typically by March 1 or May 1; AMS scholarship application by March 1 for September intake.
scholarships.durationNote: 1 year, extendable to 2 years for two-year programmes
thingsToHaveBeforeApply: Admission to a UvA Master's programme

scholarships.name: University of Auckland International Student Scholarship
scholarships.fundingSummary: Partial tuition fee scholarship (up to $10,000 NZD) for international undergraduate and postgraduate students at the University of Auckland.
benefits: Tuition fee reduction up to NZD $10,000
Open to both undergraduate and postgraduate applicants
Available for any field of study
Based on academic merit and financial need
Can be combined with other University of Auckland awards
eligibility: International student (non-New Zealand citizen or resident)
Hold a conditional or unconditional offer from University of Auckland
Strong academic record (B+ average or higher)
Meet University of Auckland English language requirements
Not currently enrolled at University of Auckland
Must pay international tuition fees
scholarships.deadlineNote: Two rounds: Round 1 closes May 1, Round 2 closes November 1. For September/February intake respectively.
scholarships.durationNote: One year (undergraduate); one year (postgraduate, can be extended)
thingsToHaveBeforeApply: Admission offer from University of Auckland

scholarships.name: University of Sydney International Scholarship (USydIS)
scholarships.fundingSummary: Full tuition fees and a living allowance for international research students undertaking a Master's by Research or PhD at the University of Sydney.
benefits: Full tuition fees for the research period
Living allowance (stipend, approximately AUD $40,109 per year in 2026)
Relocation allowance (up to AUD $5,000 for students moving from overseas)
Research support and conference travel funding
Access to University of Sydney facilities and resources
eligibility: International student (not Australian or New Zealand citizen/permanent resident)
Applied for and meet admission requirements for a Master's by Research or PhD
Excellent academic record (Honours Class 1 or 2A, or equivalent research experience)
Have a confirmed supervisor at the University of Sydney
Strong research proposal
Meet English language requirements (IELTS 6.5-7.0 overall)
documentsRequired: CV including publications and research experience
scholarships.deadlineNote: Rolling with two main rounds: Round 1 closes March, Round 2 closes July. Some faculties have separate deadlines.
scholarships.durationNote: Master's by Research: up to 2 years; PhD: up to 3.5 years
thingsToHaveBeforeApply: Strong Honours or Master's research background
Supervisor confirmed at University of Sydney

scholarships.name: Belt and Road Scholarship (China)
scholarships.provider: China Scholarship Council (CSC) / Chinese Ministry of Education
scholarships.hostUniversities: Over 200 designated Chinese universities participating in the Belt and Road Initiative programme
scholarships.fundingSummary: Full tuition, monthly stipend, accommodation, comprehensive medical insurance, and round-trip international airfare for students from Belt and Road partner countries.
benefits: Monthly stipend: Bachelors CNY 2,500, Masters CNY 3,000, PhD CNY 3,500
Chinese language preparatory course (up to 1 year)
eligibility: Citizen of a Belt and Road partner country (including Pakistan)
Non-Chinese citizen in good health
Bachelors: high school graduate, under 25; Masters: Bachelor's degree, under 35; PhD: Master's degree, under 40
Meet university admission requirements
Not a current Chinese government scholarship holder
English proficiency or Chinese proficiency (HSK 4+ for Chinese-taught programmes)
scholarships.deadlineNote: Applications open in January and close in April. Check with the Chinese Embassy in your country for specific deadlines.
scholarships.durationNote: Bachelors 4-5 years; Masters 2-3 years; PhD 3-4 years (+ Chinese language preparation if needed)

scholarships.name: Taiwan ICDF International Higher Education Scholarship
scholarships.provider: Taiwan International Cooperation and Development Fund (ICDF)
scholarships.hostUniversities: Partner Taiwanese universities (National Taiwan University, National Tsing Hua University, National Cheng Kung University, etc.)
scholarships.fundingSummary: Full tuition, round-trip airfare, on-campus accommodation, monthly living allowance, and insurance for degree study in Taiwan.
benefits: Round-trip economy airfare (to and from Taiwan)
Monthly living allowance: Bachelors NTD 15,000, Masters NTD 18,000, PhD NTD 20,000
eligibility: Citizen of an ICDF partner country (including Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, etc.)
Under 35 for Masters, under 40 for PhD
Hold the required degree for the programme level (high school for Bachelors, Bachelor's for Masters, Master's for PhD)
Meet Taiwan ICDF partner university admission requirements
Not currently studying in Taiwan
Good health (medical check required)
English proficiency (IELTS 5.5+ or TOEFL 70+)
scholarships.deadlineNote: Applications open in January and close in mid-March. Partner university admission deadlines vary.
scholarships.durationNote: Bachelors 4 years; Masters 2 years; PhD 3-4 years (including Chinese language study)

scholarships.name: KOICA Fellowship Program (South Korea)
scholarships.hostUniversities: Korean universities designated by KOICA (SNU, Yonsei, Korea University, Ewha Womans University, KAIST, etc.)
scholarships.fundingSummary: Full tuition, monthly stipend (KRW 1,000,000), round-trip airfare, accommodation, Korean language training, and medical insurance for graduate study in South Korea.
eligibility: Citizen of a KOICA partner developing country (including Pakistan)
Under 40 years of age
Bachelor's degree for Masters; Master's for PhD
At least 2 years of work experience in a relevant field
Strong academic record (GPA 3.0/4.0 or higher)
Currently employed in a position related to the programme's focus area
Commitment to return to home country after completion
English proficiency (IELTS 6.0+ or equivalent)
documentsRequired: Official academic transcripts and degree certificates
Two recommendation letters (one from employer preferred)
scholarships.deadlineNote: Applications open in February and close in March. KOICA office in your country may set an earlier deadline.
scholarships.durationNote: Masters 2 years (including 1 year Korean language); PhD 3-4 years (including 1 year Korean language)

scholarships.name: University of Calgary International Entrance Scholarship
scholarships.fundingSummary: Entrance scholarship ranging from CAD $5,000 to $40,000 for international undergraduate students entering the University of Calgary.
benefits: Scholarship amount CAD $5,000 to $40,000 (one-time or renewable)
Awarded on admission based on academic merit
No separate scholarship application required (automatic consideration)
Available for any undergraduate programme at UCalgary
Can be combined with other awards
eligibility: International student (non-Canadian) entering first year of undergraduate study
Strong academic record (high school average of 80% or higher)
Must apply for admission to University of Calgary by the scholarship deadline
Meet English language requirements (IELTS 6.5+ or TOEFL 86+)
Automatic consideration on admission — no separate scholarship application
scholarships.deadlineNote: Scholarship consideration deadline: March 1 for September intake. Apply for admission by this date.
scholarships.durationNote: One-time entrance award or up to 4 years (varies by award type)
thingsToHaveBeforeApply: University admission application submitted by March 1
